rubric.label: Fluency
rubric.desc: Speaks without long pauses; keeps the conversation moving

rubric.label: Accuracy
rubric.desc: Grammar and word forms are correct

rubric.label: Range
rubric.desc: Uses varied vocabulary, idioms and sentence structures

tracks.label: 업무 회의·이메일
scenarios: Explain a technical decision to a skeptical manager
Disagree politely with a teammate's proposal in a design review
Give a 2-minute status update and handle follow-up questions
Negotiate a deadline extension with a global partner team
Report a security vulnerability and its impact to stakeholders

tracks.label: 일상·여행 회화
scenarios: Check in at a hotel and handle a problem with the room
Order at a busy cafe and ask about the menu
Small talk with a stranger at a conference dinner
Ask for directions and transport options in a new city
Return an item at a store and ask for a refund

tracks.label: 시험(스피킹)
scenarios: OPIc-style: describe your home and a recent change you made to it
Describe a memorable trip and what you learned from it
Compare two technologies you have used and give your opinion
Talk about a problem you solved at work, step by step
Role-play: call a store to ask about a product, then handle an issue

tracks.label: 기술 문서·발표
scenarios: Explain how SBOM and VEX work to a non-technical audience
Walk through an architecture diagram of a multi-stage pipeline
Present the results of a tool benchmark and your recommendation
Explain a bug's root cause and the fix in a postmortem
Answer interview-style questions about your area of expertise

prompts.start:
You are my {{langName}} sparring partner, not a friendly tutor.
Track: {{track}}
Scenario: {{scenario}}
My level: about {{level}}. Speak ONE level above me ({{levelUp}}) with natural, idiomatic {{langName}}.

Rules:
1. Stay in the scenario. Push back on my opinions and keep asking "why" and "how" follow-ups.
2. I MUST use these expressions during the talk:
{{expressions}}
   If I forget one, steer the conversation so I need it.
3. Do NOT correct me during the conversation. Silently note every mistake for the end.
4. Keep your turns short (1-3 sentences) so I speak more than you.
5. When I say "end session", stop and wait for my review request.

Start now with your first line.
